title: Hershele and the Flying Coat
summary: Hershele hangs his patched coat on the clothesline and sits down with tea and challah, when — poo! poo-poo! — the wind lifts the coat over the tree, the roof and the cow, until it catches in the apple tree. "And what if I'd been inside it?!" cries Hershele, and runs to Rabbi Baruch to say the blessing for being saved. A funny rhyming story about wind, a coat, and giving thanks for what didn't happen.
pages:
Hershele hung his patched, beloved coat on the line,
the sun was smiling, and all around, everything was quiet and fine.
He sat in the shade with tea and challah — no worries, no rush,
not knowing that in a moment the wind would come racing — whoosh!

The wind came: Poo! — and a leaf ran off and fled.
Poo-poo! — off flew the hat. Poo-poo-poo! — and the coat... sailed off overhead!

The coat flew over the tree, and over the roof, and over the cow,
and the birds all chirped: "What's that? What's happening now?"

And at last it got caught in the apple tree's branches up high,
and hung there, sleeves spread wide and pockets puffed out, against the sky.

Hershele's mouth fell open, and he threw both hands in the air:
"And what if I'd been inside it? I'd have flown off forever, my feet dangling in the air!"

"If I'd been inside it — I'd have flown!
If I'd been inside it — I'd be hanging from a branch, all alone!
If I'd been inside it — I'd have fallen in a puddle and floated there, soaked to the bone!
And what if I'd been inside it?!"

Hershele ran to Rabbi Baruch, the wet coat in his hand,
and cried: "Rabbi, I've been saved! I want to say HaGomel, the blessing for being saved — it's very important, understand!"
"Saved from what?" asked the Rabbi, alarmed. "Tell me, what happened? Say!"
"The wind took my coat — over the roof and over the cow, far away!"

The Rabbi smiled: "But you weren't hurt — not at all, not one bit?"
"That's exactly why! I was saved from everything that didn't happen — well, very nearly, I admit!"
And what if I'd been inside it?

In the synagogue Hershele said HaGomel, grinning from ear to ear,
and the whole congregation answered: "Amen!" — so loud the heavens could hear!

The next day he hung the coat up again, and tied it with three knots — just to be sure!
The wind came: Poo-poo-poo! — and the coat just danced, and laughed, and was happy, nothing more.

Hershele sat in the shade with tea and challah — no worries, no rush,
and whispered: "And what if I'd been inside it?" — and smiled. "I'm right here. And now — there's no need to rush."
